THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C. PRAYING TO QUASH THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS IN C.C.NO.4996/2014 REGISTERED BY RESPONDENT NO.1 POLICE FOR THE OFFENCES P/U/S 498-A, 506 OF IPC AND SEC.3 OF DP ACT COMPOUNDING THE OFFENCE INITIATED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1 ON THE COMPLIANT OF RESPONDENT NO.2 WHICH IS PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE LEARNED VII ADDITIONAL CHIEF METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE AT BENGALURU.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Learned HCGP takes notice for respondent No.1/State.
Respondent No.2 has appeared voluntarily and she herself identified as complainant.

2. This petition is filed by the petitioner under section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing criminal proceeding with respect to FIR in Crime No.89/2013 registered by Rajagopalnagar Police Station,
Malleshwaram Sub-Division, Bengaluru, in C.C.No.4996/2014 for the offence punishable under Section 498A and 506 of IPC and Section 3 of Dowry Prohibition Act pending on the floor of VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.
3.

entities.text:
Rajagopalnagar Police Station,
Malleshwaram Sub-Division, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the pendency of the petition, both petitioner and respondent no.2 appeared before the Court and filed joint compromise application in I.A.No.1/2013 along with the affidavit and submits that they have already settled the issues before the Mediation Centre, Bengaluru.
As per the terms of the compromise the petitioner has already paid Rs.2 lakhs to the respondent No.2 and remaining Rs.3 lakhs is payable before the Magistrate on or before 13.03.2023.

4. Submission of both the parties are placed on record.
5.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another reported in 2012 CRI.L.J.4934, the criminal proceedings requires to be quashed.
